List issues with filters. Pass multiple status/priority/label values to filter by multiple values.

``label_match`` controls multi-``label`` semantics: ``all`` (default —
issue must carry every named label; the CLI's documented contract) or
``any`` (issue must carry at least one; used by the web UI's
multi-select filter).

Exclude filters (``exclude_label``, ``exclude_status``, ``exclude_priority``,
``exclude_issue_type``, ``exclude_assignee_id``) remove matching issues
from the result. For labels, an issue is excluded if it carries any of
the named labels. Use ``exclude_assignee_id=unassigned`` to hide
issues with no assignee.

All filter parameters work consistently whether querying by project_id or team_id.

Reject a ticket-level GATE request or REVIEW attestation, with a

The gate stays pending and the ticket does not move. A REVIEW
attestation is withdrawn, so the agent attests again; a GATE request
stays open until the requester asks again. The reason reaches the
attester (and its owner) in the inbox, the issue's activity, and the
ritual's pending view. 409 when it was already approved or rejected,

post.description:
Create a new API key. The full key is only shown once.

An agent minting a key for itself gets one linked to it whose holder
is the human behind the key it called with (CHT-1508): whoever holds
the calling key holds the new one too, so leaving the team ends both.
The holder's
membership is re-checked in the same transaction as the insert, so a
removal that commits first cannot leave behind a key its sweep
missed. An agent with no calling key on record is refused rather than
given a key nobody holds.

Callers: an agent with `can_register` (with one of its own keys), or

get.description:
Incremental inbox sync for an offline client (CHT-1607).

Across every team the user can read. Without `since`, the open entries
(read or not); with it, every entry created or changed after it, where
archived and resolved ones come back as tombstones (`state`) for the
device to drop. Ordered oldest change first. Each entry carries the
one-call `actions` its recipient can take. See InboxSyncResponse for
the client contract (`reset`, `team_ids`, repeats).

get.description: Serve the main page.

Report what commit/build is live (CHT-1294): git sha, commit time,
process start time, and the content-hash cache-busters currently
stamped onto the JS/CSS. Unauthenticated on purpose -- it's deploy
metadata, not secrets -- and fail-soft (unknown/missing, never 500).

Health check endpoint.

Beyond process liveness (this endpoint responding at all), does a
trivial DB round-trip so a broken/unmigrated database surfaces here
instead of only 500ing on the first real request (e.g. signup) --
see the seeded lifespan/migration bug this closes. Additive only:
`status` stays "healthy" for callers that only check that key/value
(cli/src/cli/system.py::health_check polls this for HTTP 200); `db`
and `version` are new.
CLI authorization page - creates API key and redirects to CLI callback.

Serve the SPA for all non-API routes.

Except ``/.well-known/*`` (CHT-1550): clients probing for discovery
documents (OAuth, OIDC, security.txt, ...) expect JSON or a 404, and
would try to parse the SPA's HTML. The documents this server does
serve are routed ahead of this catch-all.

AgentKeyResponse.title: AgentKeyResponse
AgentKeyResponse.description:
One key that authenticates as an agent, for the people who manage
it (GET /agents/{id}/keys, CHT-1508). `owner_id` is the human who
holds the key (its `holder_user_id`): whoever minted it, or for a key
the agent minted for itself, the holder of the key it called with.
It is null only for a key nobody answers for, which cannot sign in.

`legacy_self_minted` is always false since migration 0021 (CHT-1537)
and is kept so older clients still parse the response: it marked a
key the agent minted before holders were recorded, whose `owner_id`
was the agent. 0021 recorded the agent's creator as those keys'
holder, so they now list like any other key.

InboxSyncResponse.title: InboxSyncResponse
InboxSyncResponse.description:
One page of GET /inbox/sync (CHT-1607). The client contract:

* Store `next_cursor` and send it back as `since` next time. While
  `has_more` is true, fetch again at once; otherwise wait for the next
  poll or push.
* Upsert every entry by `id`; drop it when `state` is `resolved` or
  `archived`. The same entry can come more than once: the cursor stays
  a few seconds behind the newest change, so recent changes are sent
  again on the next sync.
* When `retry_after` is set, the cursor is being held back behind
  rows just sent: syncing again sooner than that many seconds returns
  the same rows. Push or user action may still sync earlier.
* When `reset` is true, the server restarted the sync (the caller's
  teams changed since the cursor was issued): clear the cache before
  applying this page, then page on as usual.
* Drop any held entry whose team is not in `team_ids` (a left or
  deleted team sends no tombstones).
* Display fields (`issue_identifier`, `document_title`, `source_user`)
  are resolved when sent. A document title or a person's name change
  re-sends the open entries that show it; anything else that changes
  them does not, so treat them as a snapshot.

PushTransport.title: PushTransport
PushTransport.description:
How the server delivers to a `push_devices` row (CHT-1604).

WEB_PUSH: standard Web Push (RFC 8030) with VAPID (RFC 8292) and an
aes128gcm payload encrypted to the device's keys (RFC 8291), POSTed
to the device's endpoint URL. UnifiedPush distributors such as ntfy
accept it. The only transport today.

A later transport (an FCM relay, CHT-1608) is a new member here and
nothing else: the column stores the member's name as text, so adding
one needs no migration, and `p256dh`/`auth` are nullable in the table
for a transport that has no per-device keys.

RitualRejectionResponse.title: RitualRejectionResponse
RitualRejectionResponse.description:
A rejected gate request or review attestation (CHT-1606).

``attested_*`` describe what was rejected: the REVIEW attestation that
was sent back (deleted on reject, so this is its only record), or for a
GATE the request that is still waiting. ``superseded_at`` is set once
the attester tried again or the gate was completed anyway.

TeamRoleUpdate.title: TeamRoleUpdate
TeamRoleUpdate.description:
Schema for updating a team member's role (CHT-1223).

PATCH /teams/{team_id}/members/{user_id} previously bound `role` as a
bare (query-string) function param, but every client (CLI included)
sends it as a JSON body -- this schema makes the body path work.
